blocks.x: Hudson, NY doesn’t do subtle in October.
The Hudson River town, perched about two hours north of NYC, was once again named one of the country’s most beautiful places to see fall foliage in Veranda’s 2026 round-up.

Once its maples, oaks, and birches hit their stride, the riverfront becomes a saturated sweep of scarlet, copper, and gold, with the Catskills rising across the water and 18th- and 19th-century architecture doing its very best impression of a movie set.
Known to many as the “Brooklyn of Upstate,” Hudson is more than a pretty leaf-peeping stop.

Its walkable core is packed with antique stores, galleries, bookstores, bars, bakeries, and destination-worthy restaurants, which means a foliage day trip can very easily turn into a full Upstate retreat.
Here’s why you should be bookmarking Hudson before peak season and how to visit properly.

Getty Images / OlegAlbinsky
Hudson’s peak foliage is expected mid- to late October
According to Veranda, Hudson’s best fall-color window falls between mid- and late October.

Timing can shift depending on rain, wind, temperatures, and how dramatically Mother Nature decides to handle the season, but current Hudson Valley foliage outlooks expect color to begin appearing across much of the region in late September before moving toward peak conditions later in October.
Before locking in a hotel, check the latest New York State fall foliage report.
It’s updated throughout the season and gives the most useful on-the-ground read of whether Hudson is still green, beginning to turn, at peak, or already shedding leaves with the rest of us.
How to see Hudson at its most colorful
The best Hudson foliage day does not require an overcomplicated schedule. It just needs a little strategic wandering!

Start with coffee and a breakfast sandwich at Kitty’s Market, then make your way along Warren Street, Hudson’s main drag, for galleries, antique shops, bookstores, and boutiques. The street has the browse-all-afternoon energy of a favorite Brooklyn neighborhood, but with fewer delivery bikes and much better mountain views.

For the photo that will make your group chat temporarily resent your ability to leave the city, head to Promenade Hill Park at the end of Warren Street. The small bluff-top park overlooks the Hudson River and the Catskills, giving you that dramatic foliage-and-water view without requiring a summit attempt.

For a more immersive leaf-peeping moment, drive about 10 minutes south to Olana State Historic Site, the Persian-inspired home and estate of Hudson River School painter Frederic Edwin Church. The property is as much an overlook as it is a historic site, with views stretching across the river toward the Catskills. Its rolling grounds, old carriage roads, and painterly sightlines make it one of the most cinematic ways to see the Hudson Valley’s autumn colors.

Art people should also add Art Omi in nearby Ghent to the plan. The 120-acre sculpture park lets visitors walk among large-scale outdoor artworks set against meadows, woodland, and big-sky views. It becomes particularly stunning once the foliage begins to turn.

Getty Images / demerzel21
Where to eat, drink, and stay
Hudson’s foliage is the reason to make the trip. Its food, drinks, and historic inns are why a Saturday day trip can suddenly become a full weekend plan.

For a proper fall dinner, book a table at Wm. Farmer & Sons, a cozy restaurant, barroom, and fourteen-room inn on South Front Street. The seasonal menu pulls from Hudson Valley farms, while craft cocktails and the intimate, copper-toned barroom make it a natural October nightcap stop.iloveny+2

For cocktails, head to The Maker Hotel, a dramatic historic property near Warren Street whose richly layered interiors are exactly the right remedy when the October air starts to bite. Even if you are not staying overnight, its bar makes a great rainy-day backup plan or a stylish final stop after sunset at the river.

Wine people should stop into Sonder, the intimate natural-wine bar just off Warren Street. It has a lively, low-lit energy that feels distinctly Hudson, slightly Parisian, and ideal for one final glass before dinner.

For an overnight stay, The Amelia is a romantic Queen Anne-style guesthouse near Warren Street. Wm. Farmer & Sons is the all-in-one choice for travelers who want their room, dinner, coffee, and nightcap in the same historic building.

Source / Angie Gaul for Historic Hudson Valley
Fall events worth planning around

Hudson’s calendar does not go quiet after summer. The town’s official events calendar is the best place to check for current performances, markets, exhibitions, live music, and seasonal programming before you go.

For an autumn weekend with even more browsing built in, the Country Living Fair takes over the Dutchess County Fairgrounds in nearby Rhinebeck from October 2 through 4. Expect hundreds of artisans, antique dealers, makers, workshops, and live Americana, folk, and bluegrass.

The Great Jack O’Lantern Blaze is another Hudson Valley classic worth knowing about. It takes place at Van Cortlandt Manor in Croton-on-Hudson, roughly an hour and 20 minutes south of Hudson, where more than 7,000 hand-carved jack-o’-lanterns light up a historic landscape.
What to know before you go
Where: Hudson, NY, in Columbia County, on the east bank of the Hudson River

From NYC: Hudson is roughly 120 miles north of Midtown. Driving generally takes a little over two hours without major traffic. You can also take Amtrak’s Empire Service from Penn Station directly to Hudson, where the station sits a short walk or quick ride from Warren Street.

Best time for foliage: Mid- to late October, according to Veranda’s 2026 fall foliage guide. Exact timing changes every year, so check the foliage tracker immediately before booking an overnight stay.
